text: The reader of this passage is led to take the three days of travel as a kind of suspended sentence, in which nothing outwardly happens, and in which everything that signifies is nevertheless happening. Obedience and horror are kept together in the story, and neither is ever suffered to prevail over the other. Faith, as it appears here, is no feeling; it has the fixed relations of a geometry. The narrator dwells upon the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire, so that the instruments of the act are named before the act itself.
